meta.title: Rossbach
meta.subtitle: Frederick the Great against the French and the army of the Holy Roman Empire, in ninety minutes.
meta.strengthNote: Army totals from Wikipedia (Duffy; Bodart); unit strengths are estimates from the battalion and squadron counts in Millar's order of battle (about 630 men per Prussian battalion, 500 per Allied battalion, 115-120 per squadron). Losses are spread across units following the narrative.
meta.method: Unit positions follow the lettered positions of a 19th-century French 1:50,000 staff plan of the battle, georeferenced against fourteen villages (RMSE 227 m), checked against two contemporary plans of 1757 and the 1911 Britannica map. Times come from Millar and from Wikipedia's account (Duffy, Showalter, Redman); the order of battle from Millar. Village positions were taken from OpenStreetMap settlement nodes and cross-checked with Wikidata; the open-cast mines, flooded pits and spoil heaps that now cover parts of the field were detected automatically and smoothed out, and the Janus and Pölzen hills restored from the period plan.
meta.notes: The v1 map placed Reichardtswerben 1.3 km and Tagewerben 1.7 km too far north-east (a geocoding error caught by the new gazetteer); everything around them has moved. Heights are exaggerated about three times; roads and woods are illustrative; the wind for drifting smoke is assumed.

phases.label: Morning
phases.title: Two camps, six kilometres apart
phases.text: Frederick's army of about 22,000 is camped between Rossbach on the left and Bedra on the right, facing west [wiki] [eb]. About 41,000 French and Imperial troops under the Prince de Soubise and the Prince of Saxe-Hildburghausen hold the heights from Branderoda to Mücheln, with Saint-Germain's advanced post on the Schortau heights overlooking the Prussian camp [wiki]. The Allies decide to march round the Prussian left and get between Frederick and the Saale crossings [wiki] [eb].
tactic: Turning movement
Marching around an enemy's flank to threaten his line of retreat. It needs speed and good scouting, and the Allies had neither [wiki].
events: Frederick's headquarters in the Goldacker manor
Saint-Germain's post overlooks the Prussian camp

phases.label: Allies march
phases.title: The allied army sets off south
phases.text: Late in the morning the Allied columns begin a long march south towards Zeuchfeld, cavalry in the lead [millar] [wiki]. Saint-Germain stays on the heights to hold the Prussians' attention [wiki]. Frederick, watching from the roof of the Rossbach manor, at first takes the movement for a retreat towards the magazines at Freyburg; at about noon he goes to dinner, leaving Captain Gaudi on the roof [wiki].
tactic: Fixing force
Saint-Germain's corps was meant to hold the Prussians in place while the main army marched round them. It never fought [wiki].
events: Saint-Germain stays to pin the Prussians
Cavalry vanguard turns east by Zeuchfeld
phases.debate: Wikipedia's account has the Allies leaving camp 'after eleven' [wiki]; Millar's plate puts the start of the march at 12:00 [millar]. The map shows noon.

phases.label: Prussians move
phases.title: Frederick strikes camp
phases.text: Gaudi reports the Allied columns turning east past Zeuchfeld; when Frederick sees hostile cavalry and infantry already approaching Pettstädt, he understands they mean to take him in flank and rear [wiki]. By 15:00 the camp is struck and the army in column [wiki]. Seydlitz takes all 38 squadrons east behind the Janus and Pölzen hills, hidden from view, with Moller's 18 guns following [wiki] [eb]. Seeing the tents fall, the Allies conclude the Prussians are retreating and hurry on [wiki].
tactic: Using dead ground
The Prussians moved along the far side of a low ridge, so the Allies could not see where they were going [wiki].
events: The Allies hurry to cut off a 'retreat'

phases.label: Guns open
phases.title: Moller's battery opens fire
phases.text: Moller's 18 heavy guns open from the Janus on the Allied cavalry, now north of Reichardtswerben and far ahead of its own infantry [wiki] [eb]. The Allied commanders take the cannonade for the cover of a retreat and press on, and their columns, attempting a wheel to the east, lose all order [wiki]. Behind the Pölzen, Seydlitz forms two lines, 20 squadrons and 18, out of sight [wiki] [gal].
tactic: Massed artillery
Heavy guns on high ground firing into troops packed in columns did terrible damage, and covered the hidden cavalry's approach [wiki].
events: 18 guns on the Janus (L on the French plan)
Seydlitz forms two lines behind the Pölzen (N)

phases.label: Seydlitz charges
phases.title: Seydlitz's charge
phases.text: At 15:30 Seydlitz brings his first 20 squadrons over the Pölzen at the gallop, knee to knee, into the Allied cavalry still strung out in column [wiki]. The Austrian cuirassiers manage to deploy and meet him; Seydlitz is wounded in the melee and sends in his other 18 squadrons, which strike the French horse at an angle [wiki]. Within about half an hour the Allied cavalry is broken [wiki] [eb].
tactic: Shock cavalry
Heavy cavalry charging in close order at the gallop hits like a wall. Seydlitz trained his men to keep formation at speed, which few cavalry of the time could do [wiki].

phases.label: Cavalry routed
phases.title: The Allied cavalry breaks
phases.text: The melee drifts south past the Allied infantry and the Allied horse streams away [wiki]. Instead of chasing it off the field, Seydlitz recalls his squadrons and rallies them in a copse about 2 km away, between Reichardtswerben and Obschütz, on the Allied flank and rear [wiki]. On the slope west of the Janus the Prussian infantry forms in echelon [wiki] [gal].
tactic: Rally and re-form
Horses and riders are blown after a charge, and scattered cavalry is useless. Rallying quickly gave Seydlitz a formed force to strike again [wiki].
phases.debate: Accounts differ on where Seydlitz rallied: Wikipedia, following Redman, puts it in a copse between Reichardtswerben and Obschütz [wiki]; the 1911 Britannica says near Tagewerben [eb]. The map places it between the two.

phases.label: Infantry fight
phases.title: The Prussian infantry advances in echelon
phases.text: The Allied infantry, freed of the cavalry, turns on the Prussian infantry threatening its left: about four battalions in line [wiki]. Instead of deploying, the Allied battalions form columns and advance with the bayonet, led by Piémont and Mailly [wiki] [eb]. Prince Henry's volleys and Moller's guns shred them; only about seven Prussian battalions fire at all, five to fifteen rounds a man [wiki] [eb].
tactic: Echelon attack
In an echelon each unit is set back from the one beside it, so the line meets the enemy one unit at a time from its strong end [wiki].
events: French columns attack with the bayonet
Prince Henry's volleys (Q on the French plan)

phases.label: Second charge
phases.title: Seydlitz strikes the infantry
phases.text: With the Allied infantry held by fire from the front, Seydlitz brings all 38 squadrons in against its flank and rear [wiki] [millar]. Three Franconian Imperial regiments throw down their muskets and run, and the French run with them [wiki].
tactic: Combined arms
Infantry fire held the enemy in front while cavalry struck the flank. Neither alone would have broken the Allied army so fast [wiki].

phases.label: Rout
phases.title: The Allied army dissolves
phases.text: The Allied army breaks and flees south-west, past Pettstädt, Storkau and Obschütz, abandoning its guns [wiki] [gal]. Seydlitz's troopers pursue until darkness makes it impossible [wiki]. Saint-Germain finally marches south from the heights to cover the retreat [millar].
tactic: Pursuit
A beaten army is most vulnerable in flight. Darkness on a November afternoon saved most of the Allied army [wiki].
events: Rout to the south-west (S and O on the French plan)

phases.label: Nightfall
phases.title: Saint-Germain and Loudon cover the withdrawal
phases.text: Saint-Germain's corps and Loudon's light troops cover the retreat as darkness falls [millar] [gal]. The battle has lasted about ninety minutes [wiki] [eb]. The Prussians have lost roughly 550 men; the Allies about 10,000 (some 6,600 French and 3,550 Imperial), about half of them prisoners, with 72 guns and 21 standards taken [wiki].
tactic: Rearguard
Fresh troops at the rear slow a pursuer and let a beaten army escape; here the coming of night mattered more [wiki].
phases.debate: Prussian losses are disputed: Frederick claimed almost none; Bodart counted about 170 dead and 430 wounded; studies of regimental records give fewer still [wiki].

units.note: Ten squadrons in reserve and twelve guarding the left flank; some were called forward for the 'pursuit' [wiki].

units.strength: Touraine, Condé, La Marine (8 bns) & horse [millar]
units.note: The Allied advanced post on the Schortau heights, which overlooked the Prussian camp [wiki]; at dusk it covered the retreat (H on the French plan) [gal] [millar].

units.name: Loudon's light troops
units.note: Austrian light troops on the Galgenberg; with Saint-Germain they covered the withdrawal at 16:45 [millar].
